question: Which of the following is the most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges as against money - based exchanges?

options.text: Bartered exchanges involve difficulty in preserving value.
Barter exchanges may result in an incorrect valuation of the goods transacted.
Barter exchanges may be imperfectly divisible.
Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barter exchanges **require a **double coincidence of wants** is the **most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges **as against **money-based exchanges**.
 
• Barter exchanges necessitate a double coincidence of wants, wherein both parties must possess items desired by the other and mutually consent to trade.
 
• In such an economy, individuals engage in the exchange of goods or services, relying on the alignment of desires between trading partners.
 
• However, barter transactions are inherently inefficient due to the requisite agreement between parties.
 
• For instance, if one person wishes to swap their laptop for a mobile phone, both parties must reach a consensus on the terms and conditions of the exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Barter** is the practice of exchanging goods or services directly between two or more parties, without involving money or monetary instruments like credit cards. 
 
• Essentially, it entails one party providing a good or service in exchange for another good or service from a different party. 
 
• Bartering operates on a straightforward premise: individuals negotiate to establish the value of their respective goods and services, then offer them to each other in a mutually agreed-upon exchange. 
 
• This system predates the existence of traditional currency, representing one of the earliest forms of trade and commerce in human history.
